title: The replica's restore job, now on production
role: You are an SRE for a self-hosted GitLab. Production backs up every night, and a replica in the other data centre restores that backup a little later, so it is always ready to take over.
brief: Yesterday, 27 February, in planned maintenance, you switched production from `gitlab-a` to the former replica `gitlab-b`. It's 02:05 UTC on 28 February. A ProbeDown alert for `gitlab-b:443` from 02:03 sits in the ticket queue. Nobody was paged; you happen to see it.

steps.situation: The web UI on `gitlab-b` doesn't answer. In chat, a night-shift user says GitLab went away in the middle of their work.
steps.evidence:
ops@gitlab-b:~$ systemctl list-timers --all | grep -iE 'backup|restore'
Tue 00:04  ...  gitlab-backup.timer   gitlab-backup.service
Tue 02:00  ...  gitlab-restore.timer  gitlab-restore.service
ops@gitlab-b:~$ journalctl -u gitlab-restore --since 01:59 | tail -2
Feb 28 02:00:01 gitlab-b restore[48121]: Restoring backup ..._2023_02_28_00_04 ...
Feb 28 02:00:03 gitlab-b restore[48121]: Unpacking backup ... done

choices.text: Check the timers and job logs on the new production host before touching GitLab
choices.why: The replica's nightly restore timer is still enabled on what is now production. At 02:00 it started restoring the 00:04 backup over live data.

choices.text: Restart GitLab to clear the slowness
choices.why: You'd interrupt a restore halfway and still not know why GitLab went down.

choices.text: Switch back to gitlab-a right away
choices.why: A second switchover at 2 a.m., before you understand the first. And gitlab-a doesn't have yesterday's changes either.

steps.situation: The restore is still running. Backups from the replica side could be restored over production too.

choices.text: Let this restore finish, and block more: disable the restore timer and the rsync that feeds backups to this host
choices.why: Disabling rsync on production was the real move, and it prevented a larger loss. The restore finished at 02:20 and GitLab then ran normally.
A half-restored database is worse than either the old or the new state, and you'd need another restore anyway.

choices.text: Restore the newest replica backup to undo it
choices.why: That backup is older still: you'd lose even more. This is exactly the loss the real team prevented.

steps.situation: GitLab is up. Work done between the 00:04 backup and the 02:00 restore is gone. It was a quiet night: one SSH session and a couple of merges.

choices.text: Announce the exact window, and ask people who pushed or merged in it to push again from their clones
choices.why: Pushed commits still live in people's clones; merge requests and comments from the window must be redone. A precise window lets people check in minutes.

choices.text: Say nothing: hardly anyone used it at night
choices.why: The few people affected discover it later and lose trust in every backup claim.

choices.text: Report "a brief outage, no data loss"
choices.why: It's false, and the merges people made in that window are proof.

steps.situation: Root cause: the setting that turns the restore timer on was set by hand per host, and nobody checked the timers after the switchover. What changes?

choices.text: Derive restore on/off from the host's role, automate switchovers, check timers after each one, and make the restore script refuse to run on the active host
choices.why: The report's actions: the role-based setting was done first; a cookbook, a timer check and a guard in the script followed as tasks.

choices.text: Add "check the timers" to the switchover wiki page
choices.why: Better than nothing, but a manual step was what failed. Put the guard in the code.

choices.text: Stop the nightly restore on the replica
choices.why: The replica is no longer ready to take over, and you no longer test your backups every night.

debrief.what_happened: On 27 February 2023 Wikimedia switched its GitLab production from gitlab1004 to gitlab2002 in planned maintenance (10:00 to 12:00 UTC). Some settings depend on whether a host is production or replica, and the restore timer setting `profile::gitlab::enable_restore` was not changed on the new production host. At 00:04 on 28 February the nightly backup ran there; at 02:00 the restore job restored that backup onto production. A ProbeDown alert fired at 02:03 and opened a task, but nobody was paged. The restore finished at 02:20. Disabling the rsync server on production stopped replica backups from being restored too, which would have lost more. Work between 00:04 and 02:00 was lost (the report says one and a half hours); the night was quiet, with one SSH connection and two merges or other actions. Actions: restore enabled or disabled automatically by instance role (done), a switchover cookbook, a timer check after switchovers, and a guard in the restore script against the active host.
lessons: Jobs that are safe on a replica can be destructive on production: tie them to the role.
After a switchover, list the timers and cron jobs on both hosts.
A destructive script should check where it runs and refuse on the primary.
Alerts on production at night should reach a person.
